chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda said: He narrated to us Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from al-Hasan ibn Haroon (the seller of fabrics) who said: I was sitting with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays asked him: 'Will the Qa'im (peace be upon him), when he rises, act in contrast to the way of Ali (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'Yes, and that is because Ali acted with leniency and forbearance because he knew that his Shia would be conquered after him, and that the Qa'im, when he rises, will act among them with the sword and captivity, because he knows that his Shia will not be conquered after him forever.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali act with leniency while the Qa'im will act with the sword?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Al-Ma'li ibn Khunays asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the strategic differences between Imam Ali and the Qa'im, highlighting a shift from leniency to decisive authority. Imam Ali adopted a posture of patience and restraint, anticipating the eventual decline of his Shia's political power, whereas the Qa'im will wield the sword and take captives, confident in the eternal supremacy of his followers. This distinction underscores the concept of *siyasa* (statecraft) adapted to the specific historical and eschatological circumstances of each leader.
